name: The Stacked Temple
description: A temple built on a temple built on a temple, and nobody left to lay the next course.
arrival: It goes up in steps, and every step is a different century's idea of what a god is owed. The lowest course is river stone laid dry, and the joints are packed with something that was once cloth. Above that, dressed sandstone. Above that, marble that came from somewhere there is no road to. The top course is a ring of scaffolding holes with nothing in them. On the bottom course, at ankle height, cut small and close together, there are names. There are more names than a village.
notes:
**The thesis: a tribute, and the ground it is standing on.** The names on the lowest course are the Jharwa dead of `event_aravali_massacre` -- and the temple was raised over them by the people whose grandfathers did it. Each age built higher and richer on the last, so what the stack actually records is guilt compounding into architecture. That reading is meant to stay uncomfortable and unresolved in both directions: Ranu and Bela were manipulated by Sira rather than acting on their own, so this is not a monument built by monsters, and it is still a monument built by the winners on the exact ground they took.

It is the map's own declared thesis made literal. `field_map_aravali` says *the ground remembers something the people here have agreed not to say* -- here the ground is saying it, in writing, at ankle height, under four hundred years of increasingly expensive stone that nobody has to crouch down to read past.

**And it did not fall to anything.** No sack, no fire, no cataclysm. The line stopped running, so the passengers stopped coming, so the alms stopped, so the purohits left, so there was nobody to pay the builders. The top course is unfinished because a timetable changed. That is the note the whole place ends on and it is deliberately smaller than the tragedy underneath it -- a memorial does not get to choose how it ends either.

**Why the near island.** `poi_first_pier` is the only other thing standing on the near island, against `poi_far_landing` and `poi_lodestone_face` on the far one, so this balances the two. It also puts the temple on the side a passenger reaches first, which is the side alms would have been given on -- the geography and the economy have to agree or the ending does not land.

**On prana and lodestone, which look like a contradiction and are not.** `mythology_the_seats_of_the_players` has the islands rise on prana vayu as humans appeared; `poi_lodestone_face` has the ore holding the island up now. Those are a beginning and a mechanism, not two answers to one question: the breath lifted the land, the ore keeps it lifted. Written down here because the next person to read both will otherwise file it as a canon error and 'fix' one of them.
